title: 2026-11-05-open-models-fitbench-and-routing-playthrough
summary: Redwood AE/SE demoed the model catalog and bench integration. Focus on selecting open models, interpreting compatibility matrix entries (kernels/quant), and routing policies for cost/latency tradeoffs. Customer concerned about SSO, SOC2, and private VPC routing for sensitive inference. Agreed to run a short bench sprint and share benchmark template + pricing. Next step: schedule pilot bench and provide security package.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share bench template, catalog export, and initial pricing by 2026-11-07
Liam O'Connor: Prepare a shortbench plan (3 tests: latency p95, cost-per-token estimate, quality pass rate) and proposed test scripts by 2026-11-09
Ava Martinez (Bluehaven): Send security contact + list of compliance questions (SOC2 artefacts, KMS) by 2026-11-06
next_steps: Run 1-week benchmark sprint on 3 open models using Redwood hosted API (Redwood to provide test harness)
Follow-up technical deep dive for private/VPC deployment with infra team (tentative 2026-11-16)
Send pricing ranges for hosted vs dedicated capacity tiers
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Ethan Brooks (Bluehaven ML Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Bluehaven Head of ML), Ava Martinez (Bluehaven Security)
Agenda: quick intros, demo catalog & benchmarks, discuss compatibility matrix and routing, security questions, next steps

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through our model catalog and how we map benches to compatibility, feel free to interrupt, let's start with quick intros
[00:18] Ethan Brooks: yeah thanks Maya, I'm Ethan, I lead model infra at Bluehaven, we're evaluating options for inference serving, main priorities latency and PII handling, also cost obviously
[00:28] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia here, product owner for the ML features, timeline is Q1 pilot and then production late Q1 or early Q2
[00:36] Ava Martinez: Ava, security lead, will be focused on compliance — SOC2, SSO, key management, also audit logs
[00:45] Maya Chen: great, quick intro from our side Liam and Priya are the engineers who own runtime and benching, Liam will show the compatibility matrix in the console
[00:54] Liam O'Connor: hi, ya, I'll start from the catalog view, bear with me if the auto captions are a little wacky, we'll open the model list and filters
[01:10] Priya Rao: we'll also show Optimize suggestions — i.e., batching and quantization profiles per model workload

[02:05] Liam O'Connor: Alright catalog — top filters are architecture, sequence length, quantization tier. Here you can see open models we've curated, each row has bench columns: p50/p95 latency on an example sequence, tokens/sec, cost estimate per 1M tokens. Note the compatibility column shows kernel map and whether we recommend INT8 or FP16 quantization for the hardware profile
[02:40] Ethan Brooks: can you clarify kernel map? is that the backend kernel selection per layer?
[02:48] Liam O'Connor: yeah it's essentially which optimized kernels we choose for that model+hw combination; sometimes it's cuBLAS, sometimes fused attention kernels. The compatibility matrix will flag 'best-fit', 'partial-fit' and 'fallback' — partial-fit means we can serve with some slower kernels or with higher memory by changing cache policy
[03:10] Sofia Alvarez: partial-fit worries me for burst traffic, what's the fallback behavior?
[03:18] Priya Rao: Good question. We have smart routing policies — you can set a policy to prefer low-latency instances, but if capacity is constrained we'll route to a cheaper variant (quantized or smaller model) and can optionally stream partial results while the longer path completes. You control thresholds by SLO or cost budget

[04:00] Ethan Brooks: is that routing within Hosted only, or does it apply for Dedicated / Private too?
[04:08] Liam O'Connor: applies across deployments. For Private/VPC you'd generally pin to a set of pools, but you can still configure in-cluster fallbacks to smaller model variants or degraded quant profiles. For strict regulatory workloads you can disable automatic fallbacks so everything stays on pinned nodes

[05:00] Ava Martinez: quick security Q — for private we need KMS integration and audit logs retained for 13 months. Support for customer-managed keys?
[05:09] Maya Chen: yes, Private supports KMS/HSM and you can bring your own keys; audit log retention is configurable — we'll share SOC2 artefacts and our security pack after this call
[05:22] Ava Martinez: great, also encryption in transit and at rest?
[05:26] Liam O'Connor: TLS in transit and disk-level encryption at rest, and KV cache contents are encrypted when persisted; note the transcript may show 'K-V cache' sometimes, but that's just the auto captions

[06:10] Maya Chen: let's demo a bench row — pick three open models: delta-lite-13B, argo-open-7B, and kora-4B (these are example curated names)
[06:22] Liam O'Connor: opening the bench comparison view — you can pin input suites, we ran our standard bench set: short dialogue, long context (2k tokens), and summarization. Here's p95 latencies on an A100-like node vs a T4-like cost-optimized node. You can see delta-lite has the best accuracy on our quality metric but higher per-token cost when FP16; with INT8 quant we lose a small quality delta but cut cost ~30%
[07:05] Ethan Brooks: how do you measure quality? is it exact-match, or we provide our own eval set?
[07:11] Priya Rao: we report both Redwood standard metrics and let you upload your prompt set. We also support Evals integration so you can track regressions across rollouts. For the sprint we'd recommend you provide 200 representative prompts for Bluehaven and we'll compute pass rates and regression alerts

[08:00] Sofia Alvarez: on the compatibility matrix I'm seeing a bunch of 'partial-fit' flags for kora-4B when sequence length >2k, is that because of kv cache or attention kernel?
[08:09] Liam O'Connor: it's mainly KV cache memory pressure in combination with a fused attention kernel that's not fully optimized for that model family on cheaper instances. Our recommendation is either reduce batch size or pin to an instance type with larger memory / different kernel set; Optimize will automatically suggest batching and caching tweaks per workload

[09:00] Ethan Brooks: can the Optimize suggestions be exported as a config we can commit to infra?
[09:05] Priya Rao: yes you can export a deployment profile (JSON) that includes batching rules, cache TTLs, quantization profile. That JSON is what our orchestration consumes for rollout and autoscale policies

[10:30] Maya Chen: pivoting to API — quick sample: POST /v1/generate with model=delta-lite-13B, you can stream responses or do structured outputs with function-calling. For bench harness we recommend streaming so you capture latency to first token and full completion time
[10:55] Ethan Brooks: is tokenization consistent across models? we're worried about cost comparisons across different tokenizers
[11:02] Liam O'Connor: tokenization differences exist; our bench normalizes by tokenizing with each model's tokenizer and reports both token counts and normalized per-1k token cost so it's apples-to-apples in the sheet

[12:00] Sofia Alvarez: about the bench sprint — what's a typical cadence and what infra do you need from us?
[12:08] Priya Rao: three tests across 5 days usually: warm-up, peak simulation, and regression/quality pass. For hosted you just provide prompts and allow us to run; for private we can push the harness into your VPC or run edge agents depending on network policy

[13:10] Ethan Brooks: network wise, we'd prefer the harness to run inside our VPC — no egress of raw prompts allowed. Is that doable?
[13:18] Liam O'Connor: yes that's private pilot mode — we run the harness in your VPC and collect only metrics (latency, token counts, quality hashes) unless you permit transcript export. We'll provide a checklist for the VPC peering and IAM roles needed

[14:00] Ava Martinez: one more compliance question — do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning?
[14:06] Maya Chen: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC and SCIM provisioning for accounts; RBAC roles in the Console map to project scopes and API keys

[15:20] Liam O'Connor: jumping back to the compatibility matrix UX — you can click into a model row and see kernel-level notes: which layers are currently using fallback kernels, memory pressure warnings, and a 'Why partial-fit' explanation with suggestions to mitigate. For example, enabling prefix KV caching reduces repeated prefix compute and lowers p95 by ~18% on long-context summarization tests

[16:05] Ethan Brooks: interesting, can you show an example where routing cuts cost during non-peak?
[16:13] Priya Rao: sure — configure a routing policy: prefer 'high-perf' pool during 9-17 PST, and 'balanced' pool off-peak; add fallback to quantized model variant if queued latency exceeds 300ms. The policy UI shows simulated cost delta and expected SLA hit rate; you can also set an absolute cost cap which triggers throttling or degraded responses

[17:30] Sofia Alvarez: about pricing — how granular is the per-token pricing for model variants vs quantized models?
[17:36] Maya Chen: priced per model variant + infra tier; quantized variants are typically 20–40% cheaper depending on quant mode. For Dedicated we do committed capacity pricing; we'll share a pricing sheet with example math for your traffic profile

[18:20] Ethan Brooks: what about vendor lock-in concerns? If we train a small model internally and want to deploy later, how portable is it to Redwood runtime?
[18:30] Liam O'Connor: We support standard model formats (Hugging Face, ONNX in some cases), and provide a migration guide. The runtime is model-agnostic but some custom ops need shim layers; we surface compatibility warnings when onboarding a new model
[18:50] Maya Chen: also note our model catalog is advisory — you can pin your own model versions in Production and use the same routing/Optimize tooling

[20:00] Priya Rao: quick demo of Console: left pane is projects, middle is model catalog, right pane is bench comparison. You can filter by compliance tags (e.g., 'pci', 'pii-safe') and see only models verified for private deployments

[21:05] Ava Martinez: how do you verify 'pii-safe' models? is that a label or an automated test?
[21:11] Liam O'Connor: it's a combination — we run static checks and a set of dynamic prompts to check for leakage; label is applied after manual review for anything used in regulated workloads

[22:00] Ethan Brooks: ok on the bench results, if a model shows small regression after quantization how do you recommend we evaluate whether the tradeoff is acceptable?
[22:08] Priya Rao: we compute quality loss per prompt and provide a pass/fail based on thresholds you set; also provide a confusion matrix and sample outputs so your SMEs can eyeball failure modes. For the sprint we'd present both a quantitative pass rate and 20 flagged samples for manual review

[24:30] Maya Chen: let's capture decisions — Bluehaven will run hosted bench sprint first on these three models, with prompts run inside Bluehaven VPC pilot harness. We'll then review results and decide whether Dedicated reserve or Private deployment is needed for production. Any objections?
[24:45] Ethan Brooks: no objections, that's the plan

[25:50] Sofia Alvarez: timeline — can you get the bench template today or tomorrow? We want to finalize internal approvals by 2026-11-10
[25:58] Maya Chen: yes I'll send bench template and pricing by 2026-11-07, Liam will follow with harness details and a suggested script

[27:00] Priya Rao: small demo note — Optimize will suggest quantization profiles but you can override per-route, per-model. We also run periodic re-evals to detect regressions when we roll new kernels or models
[27:35] Ethan Brooks: any limit on number of model variants we can pin?
[27:40] Liam O'Connor: no hard limit, but practical limits are driven by memory and orchestration complexity; we can help you curate a shortlist during the sprint

[29:00] Ava Martinez: one more — audit logs. Do logs include prompt text by default? That's a hard no for us.
[29:08] Maya Chen: default is to redact prompt text in audit logs; you can opt-in for full text if needed. For private pilots we can set retention policies and ensure only hashed or redacted prompt traces are exported

[31:00] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up, we'll attach the security pack to the follow-up email, and set up the bench sprint kickoff. Liam, Priya, any final technical points?
[31:12] Liam O'Connor: nothing major, just that when running inside your VPC we'll need a small IAM role and a volume for local cache to get accurate KV performance metrics
[31:25] Priya Rao: and we'll provide a script to reproduce the three bench phases locally if you want to run them yourselves first

[33:00] Ethan Brooks: sounds good. Also curious about fallbacks: if a model variant fails inference because of an OOM on a pinned node does Redwood automatically retry on another node?
[33:09] Liam O'Connor: yes by default we have retries with backoff and reroute to a compatible variant if available; you'd control retry policies in the deployment profile. For strict compliance you can turn off cross-region reroutes

[35:00] Maya Chen: I'll summarize after we finish Q&A — anything else from Bluehaven?
[35:08] Sofia Alvarez: just one thing — we may want a short performance SLA for the pilot so execs can sign off, can you provide expected p95 ranges for the three models?
[35:18] Priya Rao: yes we'll include expected p95 ranges in the sprint plan and show both hosted and dedicated estimates

[37:00] Ethan Brooks: competitor question — how does Redwood's routing compare to what we've seen in Vertex AI? We liked the auto-scaling but it felt opaque
[37:10] Liam O'Connor: routing in Redwood is policy-driven and surfaced in Console with simulation. We push transparency: you can see which pool is selected and why, plus cost breakdown per route. Vertex focuses on scale but less on model-variant-aware routing

[38:30] Maya Chen: ok let's lock next meeting dates. Proposed: bench kickoff 2026-11-09 and private/VPC deep dive 2026-11-16. Any conflicts?
[38:38] Ethan Brooks: those work for us

[40:00] Priya Rao: I'll add a short checklist for VPC connectivity — basically a VPC endpoint, IAM role, and security group rules, we'll also include a small troubleshooting doc

[41:15] Ava Martinez: we'll compile the compliance questions and send by 2026-11-06

[42:00] Maya Chen: perfect. Thanks everyone. Quick recap: Maya to send bench template + pricing by 2026-11-07, Liam to prepare bench plan by 2026-11-09, Bluehaven to provide prompts + compliance Qs by 2026-11-06, kickoff bench 2026-11-09. We'll follow up with calendar invites

[42:45] Ethan Brooks: thanks Maya, Liam — really helpful walkthrough
[42:50] Sofia Alvarez: thanks folks, bye
[42:53] Maya Chen: bye all

[43:00] End of recording.
